title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Hawke's Bay and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show the grape or blend, Hawke's Bay GI, and often Gimblett Gravels or Bridge Pa Triangle. Bordeaux blends may list grapes in order of share, like Merlot Cabernet. New Zealand's 85% rules apply. Screw caps are standard, even for reds.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Hawke's Bay Bordeaux blends suit lamb, a New Zealand staple, beef and venison. Syrah suits lamb with rosemary, game and peppered steak. Chardonnay suits roast chicken, crayfish and creamy fish. Serve reds at 16 to 18 degrees; good blends age 10 to 15 years.

steps.prompt: Which meat is a classic New Zealand match for Hawke's Bay reds?
steps.explanation: New Zealand lamb suits its Bordeaux blends and Syrah.

steps.body: Hawke's Bay is also known for its Art Deco town of Napier, rebuilt after a 1931 earthquake.

steps.prompt: Good Hawke's Bay red blends can age 10 to 15 years.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show the GI and often Gimblett Gravels
Its reds suit lamb, beef and venison
